title: malloc and free
summary: Stack memory disappears when a function returns and must have a size known in advance. The heap gives memory of any size that lasts until you free it. malloc returns NULL when it fails, calloc clears the memory, and every malloc needs exactly one free - never zero, never two.

cards.a:
When the program calls free on it (or the program ends)

C has no garbage collector.

cards.q: What does malloc return when it cannot allocate?
Why is int *p = malloc(n * sizeof *p) a good pattern?
cards.a:
The size follows the pointer's type automatically

Change int to long and the allocation is still right.

Allocated memory that is never freed

The memory stays taken until the program exits.
